record.paper_title: Research Problems on Relations Between Nijenhuis Geometry and Integrable Systems
record.original_question: Generalize the explicit metric-construction formula from [17] to arbitrary coordinates x^1,...,x^n under the assumption that one is given an explicit conservation law f(x^1,...,x^n) in those coordinates.

evidence.quote: Problem 4.5. Generalise the above mentioned formula from [17] to an arbitrary coordinate system x1, . . . , xn assuming that in this coordinate system we have a conservation law given as an explicit function f(x1, . . . , xn).

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Setting. Let $L=(L^i_j(x))$ be a smooth field of $(1,1)$-tensors (an operator field) on a smooth $n$-dimensional manifold $M$. A smooth function $f:M\to\mathbb{R}$ is called a conservation law of $L$ if the 1-form $L^{*}df$ is closed, i.e. if in any local coordinates $x^1,\dots,x^n$ one has
$$\partial_i(L^k_j\,\partial_k f)=\partial_j(L^k_i\,\partial_k f).$$
A pseudo-Riemannian metric $g$ on $M$ is said to be geodesically compatible with $L$ if $L$ is $g$-self-adjoint and the pair $(g,L)$ produces, via the standard construction, a hierarchy of geodesically equivalent metrics; equivalently, the Levi-Civita connection $\nabla$ of $g$ satisfies the geodesic compatibility equation
$$\nabla_k L^i_j=\tfrac12\bigl(\delta^i_k\,\partial_j\operatorname{tr}L+\delta^i_j\,\partial_k\operatorname{tr}L\bigr)-\tfrac12\bigl(g_{jk}\,g^{is}\partial_s\operatorname{tr}L\bigr).$$

Known formula (in companion-form coordinates). Suppose $L$ is $\mathrm{gl}$-regular and that in some local coordinate system the operator $L$ is in second companion form. Then, given a single explicit conservation law of $L$ written in those coordinates, there is an explicit closed-form expression that produces a pseudo-Riemannian metric $g$ geodesically compatible with $L$.

Problem. Generalise this construction to an arbitrary coordinate system: assume that on an open subset of $M$ one is given the components $L^i_j(x^1,\dots,x^n)$ of a $\mathrm{gl}$-regular operator $L$ in arbitrary coordinates $x^1,\dots,x^n$, together with an explicit smooth function $f(x^1,\dots,x^n)$ that is a conservation law of $L$ in these coordinates. Produce an explicit, coordinate-free (or at least coordinate-independent) formula that constructs from the data $(L,f)$ a pseudo-Riemannian metric $g$ geodesically compatible with $L$, and which reduces to the known companion-form formula when $L$ is brought to second companion form.
artifact.status_search_result: The problem appears in a 2024 collection of research problems on Nijenhuis geometry as an open research problem. The known explicit formula constructs a geodesically compatible metric from a conservation law only in second-companion-form coordinates; a coordinate-free generalisation is requested but no published solution was found in the search results.

status_evidence.snippet: Problem 4.5. Generalise the above mentioned formula to an arbitrary coordinate system assuming we have a conservation law given as an explicit function.

status_evidence.title: Nijenhuis geometry IV: conservation laws, symmetries and integration
status_evidence.snippet: Discusses conservation laws and explicit metric construction in companion-form coordinates for gl-regular Nijenhuis operators.
status_evidence.claim: The companion-form metric formula referenced in the problem is the one whose coordinate-free generalisation is sought.
